title: Google's A2A protocol joins Agentic AI Foundation, sharing a roof with MCP
subtitle: The Linux Foundation-run AAIF now hosts both major open standards for agent interoperability, with 250-plus members including AWS, Anthropic, Microsoft, and OpenAI.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google Cloud formally donated its Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol to the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation on August 20, placing it under the same neutral governance as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), which the foundation absorbed earlier this year. AAIF now counts more than 250 members, up from 49 a year ago, with platinum signatories AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. Both protocols keep their open-source licenses and technical steering committees, but neither is a single vendor's project anymore.

A2A and MCP address different layers of the same problem — how do agents built by different vendors do useful work together. MCP describes how an agent connects to a tool, resource, or data source. A2A describes how two agents talk to each other: negotiating tasks, exchanging structured messages, and coordinating over long-running work. Putting both under one foundation means the same governance body decides schema changes, security requirements, and conformance tests. For enterprise buyers, that reduces the risk of a protocol fork the way OpenTelemetry and CNCF did for observability and Kubernetes.

The move also settles a question the industry has been asking since MCP shipped: was Anthropic going to own the primary agent-integration layer, or was there room for a Google-backed alternative to complicate the picture? Both are now equally 'not owned' — which is what enterprise procurement teams have been waiting for before green-lighting deeper agent integrations. It also aligns with the AWS AgentCore update that landed the same day, which points at AWS running MCP and A2A as first-class runtime protocols inside Bedrock.

A note for learners: an open standard becomes real when the people who could have shipped a proprietary alternative stop trying. Two years ago, most vendors would have preferred their own protocol over anyone else's. That every major cloud and lab now signs up to AAIF as platinum members is the signal — this is where interoperability is going to be arbitrated. If you are learning to build agents, MCP and A2A are the two names to know, and their specs are the authoritative reference now, not any single vendor's docs.
